title: EventIdentityResult
description: Canonical structured output for the Event Identity call. Generated from src/lib/ai/event-identity/contract.ts — do not hand-edit. `identity` is the creative brief, `suppliedFacts` quotes the host verbatim or is null, `clarification` carries either up to three creative questions or one boundary question. spec.md §7.5, §7.6b; docs/model-contracts.md §4.

creativeDirection.description: Concise 1-3 sentence creative thesis. No renderer implementation choices.

toneKeywords.description: Ranked/curated tone adjectives or short phrases with minimal synonym redundancy.

colorsExplicitlyConstrained.description: True only when the host explicitly narrows/requires/excludes palette families.

requiredColors.description: Hard color requirements in short natural language; preserve exact user hex strings.

avoidColors.description: Explicit color exclusions. An exclusion is absolute and covers near neighbours.

dominanceNotes.description: How palette families should dominate/recede; empty string when unspecified.

toneExplicitlyConstrained.description: True only when the host explicitly constrains light/mid/dark tonal space.

compatibleTonalDirections.description: Ranked best-first compatible tonal directions. Do not pad with incompatible values.

compatibleFamilies.description: Ranked best-first compatible design families. A family is a compositional character.

compatibleTypographyCategories.description: Ranked compatible broad typography categories, not a font choice.

visualMotifs.description: Natural-language motif ideas, not renderer motif IDs.

textureDirection.description: Tactile/visual texture character. Never an image asset.

typographyDirection.description: Typographic character/hierarchy, not a raw font-family choice.

hostConstraints.description: AUTHORITATIVE, and narrow. A prohibition, an explicit requirement of a specific thing, or a correction the host made — grounded in an explicit phrase from their own words and kept verbatim or near-verbatim. Positive style direction is NOT a constraint: a named aesthetic or a tone adjective the host wants shapes the brief itself (creativeDirection, toneKeywords, palette), which is where later stages read it. If interpretation was needed to get here it is creativeGuidance. Empty is the common and correct answer.

creativeGuidance.description: ADVISORY. Your own creative recommendations. Later design stages may reconsider, override or evolve any of these when they find something better. This is where your taste belongs — never in hostConstraints.

inspirationSummary.description: Compact summary of inspiration evidence; exactly 'No visual inspiration supplied.' when none exists.

identity.description: The creative brief. Inference is expected and generous. Carries no operational data.

hostNames.description: Who is hosting, as written. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

honoreeName.description: The NAME of whoever the event is for, as written — their name, or the personal name they actually go by. A relationship is not a name. A nickname, title, rank, role, handle or joke is not a name either WHEN the host presents it as a label attached to the person rather than the name they go by; a nickname someone actually goes by is their name. The lexical category of the term decides nothing, and neither does whether a word looks name-like — what decides is the role the host gives it. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

honoreeDescriptionText.description: How the host DESCRIBED who the event is for — 'my nephew', 'our neighbour', 'for the twins'. Populate this even when honoreeName is also present: 'my nephew Arthur' gives honoreeName 'Arthur' and honoreeDescriptionText 'my nephew'. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred, and never a reason to impose a stereotyped palette.

eventType.description: The kind of GATHERING the host named — a dinner, a shower, a birthday. A theme, an aesthetic or a mood is never an event type, however literally the host stated it. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

dateText.description: The date exactly as written, however partial. Never expanded into a fuller date. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

timeText.description: The time exactly as written. Do not reformat: '1pm' stays '1pm'. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

venueText.description: The venue as named or described. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

addressText.description: A street address, only if the host gave one. Never derived from a described place. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

localityText.description: Town/city/region as written. A city named as aesthetic flavour is not a location. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

rsvpDeadlineText.description: The RSVP deadline as written. Quoted from the host verbatim, or null. Never inferred.

suppliedFacts.description: What the host actually said. Every value is a quotation or null.

needed.description: True when and only when `questions` is non-empty. Prefer zero questions.

kind.description: 'creative' for a question of taste, governed by the five conditions. 'boundary' for a decision that is not yours to make. Every question declares which; a question that fits neither must not be asked.

question.description: For 'creative': a question about taste. For 'boundary': ask the host to state the boundary they can legitimately affirm as settled — never to authorize something on another person's behalf, and never offering to decide it yourself. Never logistics — never a date, time, venue, address, guest count or budget — and never a low-level design choice.

whyItMatters.description: For 'creative': how the answers would diverge creatively. For 'boundary': the position the brief would otherwise take on someone's behalf, and why it is not yours to take. Not shown to the host as written.

label.description: The option as the host would read it.

isDefer.description: True on the single 'You decide' / 'Surprise me' option a creative question must offer. Always false on a boundary question: that decision is the host's, and you may not offer to take it. A conservative option the host picks (leaving the matter out, keeping it unspecified) is a real choice, not a defer.

options.description: Answer options. A creative question has exactly one isDefer: true; a boundary question has none, because that decision is the host's.

questions.description: Usually none. Either up to three creative questions, or exactly one boundary question and nothing else — a boundary must be settled before the brief is authoritative, and asking taste questions alongside it turns one question into an intake form.

clarification.description: Whether a question must be put to the host before designing. Usually not — zero is the normal and most common answer.

$comment: event_identity_schema_v5: each clarification question declares a `kind` — `creative` or `boundary` — and defer semantics follow it. v4: `designConstraints` splits into `hostConstraints` (authoritative, host-grounded) and `creativeGuidance` (advisory), and `suppliedFacts` gains `honoreeDescriptionText`. v3 introduced the envelope: `identity` plus `suppliedFacts` (quoted or null, never inferred) and `clarification`. Provider strict mode receives the reduced projection in event-identity-result.wire.schema.json; the application always runs the full contract (docs/model-contracts.md §3).
